title: Trees, binary search trees and traversal
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its constraints.
Trace the example and reason about its data flow.
Identify complexity, boundary or safety considerations.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: A tree is a hierarchical data structure made of nodes connected by edges. A binary tree gives each node at most two child links. A binary search tree maintains an ordering invariant that guides lookup and insertion; performance depends on tree shape.
understand.whyItMatters: Trees model hierarchical data and can support efficient operations when balanced. An unbalanced search tree can degrade toward linear-time operations.
understand.analogy: Treat an algorithm or data structure as a set of operations that must preserve a clearly stated contract.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace formal complexity analysis, C object rules or algorithm preconditions.

explain.narrative:
A tree is a hierarchical data structure made of nodes connected by edges. A binary tree gives each node at most two child links. A binary search tree maintains an ordering invariant that guides lookup and insertion; performance depends on tree shape.

Before implementation, state input constraints, empty-case behaviour, ownership and invariants. Compile with warnings and test representative, boundary and failure cases.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The search follows the left child for a smaller key and the right child for a larger key. The invariant must be maintained by insertion and deletion operations.

practise.guidedTask: Trace a search through a small tree and record each visited key.
practise.independentTask: Implement insertion and in-order traversal for a binary search tree. Include allocation-failure and cleanup handling.
hints: An in-order traversal of a valid binary search tree visits keys in sorted order.
A plain binary search tree is not guaranteed to remain balanced.
Every allocated node needs an ownership and release strategy.
